chapter: Ensemble, harmony and the Ory band
title: Ory's discipline with modern players
summary: Allen recalls an Ory interview about reading parts; DeVore says Ory gets his sound even from modern musicians.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Well, I listened to the Ori interview that Naz did. Did you ever hear that one? No. Well, Ori talks about it and he says all that was so beautifully arranged and everything except that he wasn't reading his part. No, Ori knew all that stuff. Ori knew all that stuff. Sure. But some of it was new to him, I'm sure. But he knew it almost immediately. He could just listen and grab it right away somehow. Yeah, Ori... Because he had such an ear, or had such an ear, I don't know. I haven't heard his recent records.

Yeah, no, all his... I haven't heard the more up to date stuff. I've heard some of it. Some of it's very good. Ori has got kind of a contemporary sound to his band. It's fantastic. Ori is really a disciplinarian because he can take the modern cats and make them play the way he wants them to. So his bands, even with modern piano players, have that common Ori sound. I can't understand it. You know, taking guys like Marty Marcella and... Well, Darnell Howard, of course, who always played in the wrong style. But other guys, and yet get kind of the same sound. I have an approximation of it. And I think Ori just drove it into them.
